3.  Findings to Continue to Hold Remote Teleconference/Virtual City Council Meetings
  Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361
  At the November 16, 2021 City Council meeting, the City Council made findings pursuant
  to Assembly Sill 361 to continue to meet remotely. To continue this practice, it is required,
  that the City Council determine that the COVID-1 9 state of emergency proclaimed by the
  Governor still exists and has been considered by the City Council in deciding to continue
  to have teleconference meetings and that state or local officials have imposed or
  recommended measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, and
  that as a result of the COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent
  risks to the health or safety of attendees. Because these findings must be made every
  thirty (30) days, the City Council will have to make these findings at its upcoming June 8,
  2022 meeting and thirty (30) days thereafter.
  Recommended Action
  Determine that the COVID-1 9 state of emergency proclaimed by the Governor still exists
  and has been considered by the City Council in deciding to continue to have
  teleconference meetings and that state or local officials have imposed or recommended
  measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, and that as a result
  of the COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent risks to the
  health or safety of attendees.

4.  Federal Grant Policies and Procedures Manual
  During the Fiscal Year 2020 Audit, Davis Farr LLP identified the lack of a written policy
  relative to Federal Awards as required by Uniform Guidance a significant deficiency on
  internal control over compliance.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt the Federal Grant Policies and Procedures Manual.

5.  Avalon Harbor Waste Tank Pump-Out Float Contract Price Increase
  On July 20, 2021 the City Council directed the City Manager to negotiate a contract for
  procurement of the assets required with Diversified Composites Inc., to complete the
  Waste Pump-Out Freshwater Fill-Up Float Replacement Project. Staff were recently
  notified due to supply chain issues, the cost of materials from Diversified Composites had
  increased.
  Recommended Action
  Approve a contract price increase of $37,485.00 for the Waste Pump-Out and Freshwater
  Fill-Up Float Replacement Project with Diversified Composites Incorporated.

6.  Approve the Resolution Supporting Submittal of an Application to the State of California’s
  State Active Transportation Grant Program Cycle 6
  Since 2018, work has proceeded on developing the construction contract documents to
  implement the reconstruction of the five corners intersection. It is known that existing
  grant funds are not adequate to complete the project. Another round of State ATP Cycle
  funds has been announced.
  Recommended Action
  (1) Approve the Resolution supporting the ATP Cycle 6 grant application. 2) Approve
  the submittal of the ATP Cycle 6 grant application for the Five-Corners Project.

7.  Approval of an Additional One-Time $50 Commuter Book Subsidy for the Month of June
  2022 and Extension of Regular $85 subsidy through December 31, 2022
  The City of Avalon annually applies for Proposition A Incentive Funds through the Los
  Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro). The City has received
  $1,000,000 in Proposition A Incentive Funds annually over the last several fiscal years,
  with $700,000 earmarked for the commuter subsidy program.
  Recommended Action
  Approve an additional one-time $50 commuter book subsidy for the month of June 2022
  and extend the existing regular $85 subsidy through December 31, 2022.

GENERAL BUSINESS

8.  Consideration of Transportation Permit— Sara Mintz and Juan Saldana, dba Avalon Local
  Tour
  On May 5, 2022 Sara Mintz and Juan Saldana submitted a Transportation Permit
  application to perform guided autoette tours. The proposed route includes areas from
  Pebbly Beach Road, Mt. Ada, Avalon Canyon Road, Wrigley Memorial, Country Club
  Drive, Stage Coach Road, Casino Way and Descanso Beach.
  Recommended Action
  Discuss and provide direction to Staff. If consensus to approve is reached make the
  affirmative finding that the criteria set forth in Avalon Municipal Code Section 5-14.04 has
  been meet.

SUBJECT:  Findings to Continue to Hold Remote Teleconference/Virtual City
  Council Meetings Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Determine that the COVID-19 state of emergency proclaimed
by the Governor still exists and has been considered by the City Council in deciding to continue
to have teleconference meetings and that state or local officials have imposed or recommended
measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, and that as a result of the
COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent risks to the health or safety
of attendees.

REPORT SUMMARY: Traditionally, the Brown Act allows for teleconference or virtual meetings,
provided that the physical locations of the legislative body’s members joining by teleconference
are posted on the agenda, that those locations are open to the public and that a quorum of the
members is located within its jurisdiction. Newly enacted AB 361 provides an exception to these
procedures in order to allow for fully virtual meetings during proclaimed emergencies, including
the COVID-19 pandemic.

Since March of 2020 and the issuance of Governor Newsom’s Executive Order N-29-20, which
suspended portions of the Brown Act relating to teleconferencing, the City Council has had virtual
meetings without having to post the location of the legislative body members attending virtually.
Most public agencies have been holding public meetings using virtual platforms since this time.
In June of 2021, Governor Newsom issued Executive Order N-08-21, which provided that the
exceptions contained in EQ N-29-20 would sunset on September 30, 2021.

On September 10, 2021, the Legislature adopted AB 361, which allows public agencies to hold
fully virtual meetings under certain circumstances without the posting of the agenda from each
location a legislative body member is attending. Governor Newsom signed the bill into law on
September 16, 2021. Because it contained an urgency provision, it took immediate effect.

Specific Findings Required underAB 361

Under AB 361, the City Council can hold virtual meetings without providing notice of the City
Council’s teleconference location if the City Council makes the determination that there is a
Governor-proclaimed state of emergency, which the City Council will consider in their
determination, and one of two secondary criteria listed below exists:

  1. State or local officials have imposed or recommended measures to promote social
  distancing in connection with COVID-19; or

   2. The City Council determines that requiring a meeting in person would present an
  imminent risk to the health or safety of attendees.

COVID-19 continues to present an imminent threat to the health or safety of members of the
public, and the Governor’s declaration of a COVID-19 emergency still exists. Although vaccines
are now widely available, many people in the State and County are still not fully vaccinated and
remain susceptible to infection. The disease can still spread rapidly through person-to-person
contact and those in close proximity. Further, more contagious variants of the disease are now
present in the State and County, the most predominant of which is a new variant of the Omnicron
variant. The County of Los Angeles recently re-instituted some mandates given the rise in cases
and deaths nationally. The City’s economy is dependent upon visitors to the island, the presence
of which, increases the likelihood of transmission of the disease. Also, having members of the
public attend council meetings at locations where council members are in attendance due to their
desire to avoid exposure to COVID-1 9 poses an imminent risk to the health or safety of attendees.

Re-Authorization is Required Within 30 Days

The City Council made the findings listed above at its May 3, 2022 City Council meeting.
Consistent with the provisions of Government Code Section 54953(e), the findings must be made
every 30 days “after teleconferencing for the first time” under AB 361. Thus, if the City Council
desires to continue to meet remotely without having to post the location of each teleconference
location, the City Council must again find that the COVID-19 emergency still exists and that one
of the two following findings can be made: that state or local officials have imposed or
recommended measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19. or, that a
result of the COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent risks to the health
or safety of attendees. Because these findings must be made every thirty (30) days, the City
Council will have to make these findings at its upcoming June 8, 2022 meeting and thirty (30)
days thereafter.

It is recommended that the City Council make these findings.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City Council will
have to follow the Brown Act provisions that existed prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: That the City Council make the findings under AB 361 at its June 8,
2022 City Council meeting.

2019-002; controls over Strengthening Internal Controls

During our testing of internal controls surrounding cash receipts, cash disbursements, and
payroll, we noted the following:

  •  For cash receipts, the individual responsible for the collection of customer payments
  has the ability to modify customer data. We also noted that the individual who
  prepares the bank deposits and collects cash receipts has the ability to post receipts
  to the general ledger.

  •  For cash disbursements, we noted that access to the vendor database was not
  restricted and accounts payable personnel had the ability to add new vendors
  without review.

  •  For payroll, we noted that the employees that process payroll have the ability to add
  employees to the payroll system.

Recommendations

To ensure proper segregation of duties, we recommend the following:

  •  The individual responsible for cash receipts should be prohibited from access to the
  customer database.  In addition, the person responsible for the collection of
  payments should be prohibited from posting these transactions to the general ledger.

  •  The ability to add, delete or modify vendor data should be segregated from accounts
  payable personnel.

  •  The ability to add employees should be segregated from those that process payroll.

Management’s Resnonse

Management agrees with this finding and has already taken steps to ensure proper
segregation of duties. Individuals responsible for cash receipts no longer have system
access to post transactions to the general ledger. The Finance Director is currently working
with software vendors to implement similar segregations of duties for accounts payable and
payroll processes.

Status

This finding is considered cleared.

procurement, per the City’s purchasing policy, of two peristaltic pumps, two water supply
stanchions, and a pump alarm system from KECO Pump & Equipment that meets the
specifications for the Harbor Waste Pump-Out Dock, for a total not to exceed $56,440.

REPORT SUMMARY: On April 2, 2019, the City Council accepted a funding award from the
Department of Boating and Waterways to support the replacement of the Harbor Waste Pump-
Out Dock. The total grant award was $196,200. The dock float, waste tank pumps, and water
filling equipment would be included within the scope of the grant agreement.

On November 10, 2020 City Council authorized the solicitation of a request for bids to
construct the complete Waste Pump-Out Dock. No bids were received by the published
deadline, therefore, on July 20, 2021, City Council authorized the City Manager to negotiate a
contract for procurement of the dock float. It was understood that the supplies & equipment for
the dock would be purchased & installed by City Staff per the City’s procurement policy.

According to the AMC Sec.3-4.111(b) Sole Source Vendors, When there is only one source
that provides the necessary services, goods and equipment to ensure compatibility with
existing City services, goods or equipment, or the services, goods or equipment are proprietary
in nature, the City may procure the goods or services from the sole source.”

KECO. Inc. dba Keco Pump & Equipment is the sole provider of KECO pumps and parts.
While Keco does work with authorized representatives, all purchases are made directly
through Keco. City Staff requests KECO, Inc. be designated a sole source vendor.

The total expenditure is comprised of three elements, with the majority of this expenditure are
the peristaltic pumps, which total $47,500. This type of pump is required for this application
due to several factors. They are more environmentally safe for our harbor since they are not
prone to leaks. They are also much more efficient, and have very low maintenance costs
compared to other style of pumps. Finally, these pumps are able to handle various fluids &
debris that are often found in marine holding tanks whereas other pumps cannot handle these
items.
 The other two elements of the expenditure are two water supply stanchions totaling
approximately $8500 and a tank alert system totaling approximately $440.

Staff is requesting authorization to procure the peristaltic pumps, water supply stanchions, and
alarm system from KECO Pump & Equipment for an amount not to exceed $56,440.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Total expenditure is not to exceed $56,440 which is included in the grant
that was previously awarded totaling $196,200. This will be applied towards CIP project code
207013 (account 10470-6648).

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: Project will be further
delayed searching for other equipment that is likely not available due to specific pump
requirements as previously mentioned.

policy.

SUBJECT:  Approval of an Additional One-Time $50 Commuter Book Subsidy
  for the Month of June 2022 and Extension of Regular $85 subsidy
  through December 31, 2022

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Approve an additional one-time $50 commuter book subsidy for
the month of June 2022 and extend the existing regular $85 subsidy through December 31,
2022.

REPORT SUMMARY: The City of Avalon annually applies for Proposition A Incentive Funds
through the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro). The City has
received $1,000,000 in Proposition A Incentive Funds annually over the last several fiscal years,
with $700,000 earmarked for the commuter subsidy program, and $300,000 earmarked for the
City’s land transit system. In addition to these annual funds, the City received an additional
$364,878 in Coronavirus Response and Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act (CRRSAA)
funds through the Proposition A Incentive Program. These CRRSAA Funds must be spent in the
current fiscal year for the City’s commuter or land transit programs and cannot be used for capital
improvements.

Prior to the pandemic. from July 2016 through February 2020, the City subsidized approximately
800 commuter books per month. In response to the initial pandemic-related restrictions on non
essential travel, subsidized commuter book activity decreased to approximately 300 books per
month from the period of March 2020 through May 2020. From June 2020 through December
2021, commuter activity was down approximately 25% from pre-pandemic levels, with the City
subsidized approximately 600 commuter books per month. As a result of the CRRSAA Funds
and the decreased commuter activity, Staff recommended increasing the regular commuter book
subsidy from $70 to $85 to offset the impact of operator fare increases to residents and an
additional one-time $100 subsidy for the month of January 2022 in order to fully utilize these
funds. City Council approved Staff recommendations at the December 7, 2021 City Council
Meeting.

During the month of January 2022, the City subsidized 2,340 commuter books totaling $435,734
in subsidy expenditures. As a result of the additional one-time $100 subsidy, commuter book
purchases decreased to approximately 300 books per month for February 2022 through April
2022. Through April 2022, the City has spent $804,987 on the commuter subsidy program with
a further $259,891 available to spend over the last two months of the fiscal year. Staff
 recommends offering an additional one-time $50 subsidy for the month of June 2022 in order to
fully utilize awarded funds in the current fiscal year. It is difficult to assess the increased subsidy’s
impact on resident commuter demand and it is possible that the increased subsidy could result
in the subsidy costs exceeding available funds, requiring General Fund reserves to cover any
excess amounts. Staff does not anticipate this scenario at the proposed subsidy level but
expenditures would exceed available funds by approximately $100 thousand if subsidized
commuter book sales matched January 2022 levels.

Staff will continue to monitor activity to assess whether the increased subsidy amount is
sustainable based on commuter activity and recommends extending the current regular subsidy
amount of $85 per commuter book through December 2022. Staff will also continue to work with
Metro to identify any additional pandemic-related assistance eligible for assignment under the
Proposition A Incentive Program in future fiscal years.

could then result in a required subsidy from the General Fund for amounts in excess of
Proposition A Incentive Funds.

to utilize CRRSAA Funds that are required to be spent in the current fiscal year.
